newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: STORK OPTIMISTIC ABOUT AVIATION UNIT.
newsitem.headline: STORK OPTIMISTIC ABOUT AVIATION UNIT.

text.p: Industrial systems and services group Stork NV said on Tuesday it was optimistic about the growth prospects of its aviation activities, acquired last year from bankrupt aircraft maker Fokker .
"We have the expectation that we are only at the beginning of a further dynamic expansion in this market," Stork chairman Jan Hovers told a news conference on Stork's 1996 results.

He said that the newly acquired Fokker Aviation unit had brought in about 10 million in net profits last year on turnover of about 550 million. The unit's turnover is expected to rise to 800 million guilders in 1997 and grow further in later years.

Hovers said 1996 had been a transition year for Fokker Aviation and profitability was seen improving there. Parts of the aircraft maintenance and components group that were loss-making in 1996 were now back in the black, he said.

Contacts with aircraft makers and airlines have been built up. Everywhere in the world where Fokker aircraft are used, Stork is planning to expand its activities, possibly through takeovers, board member Aad Veenman added.
Hovers said a number of airlines are considering contracting out their maintenance activities, which would offer Stork opportunities to expand.
Plans to expand the aviation business would certainly be given priority within Stork in the years ahead, Hovers said.
Earlier, Stork posted 1996 net profit of 137 million guilders, up more than 26 percent from 1995's 108 million. Net earnings per share grew by almost 24 percent to 4.58 guilders.
Stork said operating results at its industrial systems and components division had stabilised at 134 million guilders on a two percent higher turnover of 1.97 billion guilders.
Thanks to Fokker Aviation's components units, the mix of the components group's turnover had changed drastically and the quality of this turnover had clearly improved, Stork said.
In the industrial services division, the 1996 operating profit surged to 47 million guilders from 18 million on 35 percent higher turnover of 2.95 billion guilders.
Stork received 4.8 billion guilders in new orders in 1996, up 3.4 percent from the year-earlier level.
The company expects profits to show a further rise in 1997.
"The order levels give us a sound basis for our expectation that a clear profit rise can be realised in 1997," financial manager Hans van den Boogaard said.
